observations.body: Paul appeals for bodies to be presented as a living, holy, acceptable sacrifice and for minds to be transformed rather than conformed.
observations.label: Living bodies become a reasonable sacrifice

observations.body: The passage presents mercy, body, living gift, worship, transformed mind, testing, and divine will as the scene's observable response or movement.
observations.label: mercy, body, living gift, worship, transformed mind, testing, and divine will

observations.body: The passage places living sacrifice beside mercy, body, living gift, worship, transformed mind, testing, and divine will.
observations.label: living sacrifice

payload.posture: Read Romans 12:1–2 as evidence about sacrifice, keeping its action, claim, context, and limits distinct.
payload.tension: the metaphor concerns lived bodily allegiance, not self-killing
payload.title: Living bodies become a reasonable sacrifice
